rationale: B wins because it finds the sharper reporter question A walks past: "Liquid Death says it's profitable. The new store tests what that word covers." That is a real CPG finance story if tightened to contribution-margin profitability, not net profitability. A is cleaner, but it spends one slot on "A canned-water brand says it has given $4.2M to clean-water charities. Here's what that buys." and then admits "Why now: Weak on its own." Good honesty; bad slot economy.
gaps_in_A: "Liquid Death opens a store that sells almost no water" overclaims the product mix. The update says merch, limited-edition canned water, and events; it does not give SKU split, floor share, or sales mix.

"A canned-water brand says it has given $4.2M to clean-water charities. Here's what that buys." is thin as a standalone angle, and A knows it: "Why now: Weak on its own." Tie it to B Corp accountability or kill it.

A refuses "Liquid Death is profitable and proving the challenger-brand model works" correctly, but then misses the better finance angle: contribution-margin profitability versus a fixed-cost flagship with net profit undisclosed.

"The standard just got a stress test" is a strong frame, but "the prevailing belief is that packaged single-serve water is the category sustainability certification exists to discourage" imports a premise that needs outside proof.
gaps_in_B: "Liquid Death says it's profitable" is dangerous shorthand. The fact is contribution-margin profitability with net profit undisclosed; a finance reporter will notice the missing adjective before the coffee cools.
"Liquid Death's first store is a merch shop that also sells water" overstates the available evidence. The update lists merch and limited-edition cans, but does not prove merch is dominant.

The first two kept angles overlap: "what a single owned store is for" and "what the brand is" both live off the same store-as-brand-asset idea. Keep both only if merch revenue or store strategy data supports the split.
"This reporter will want the certification to have cost something" is the right skeptical question, but don't imply operational changes happened until the B Corp assessment or company confirms them.
